home.title: Design, simulation and security of wireless networks for educational CubeSats and CanSats
home.lead: Explore at your own pace how a low-cost educational satellite communicates: from LoRa theory to a stratospheric balloon mission transmitting live.
home.diagramLabel: Atmosphere profile with a high-altitude balloon and its radio link to the ground
home.modulesLead: Discover at your own pace: each module is a gateway to knowledge. Start wherever your curiosity takes you.
home.meditLead: This ODC follows the Transmodern Digital Educational Model (MEDIT): learners manage their own path. There are no tests or scores, only content, simulation and practice to build and replicate.

principles.d: Theory, visualization, simulation and guides live in one place.
The ODC is the tangible result of the ESTRATOSAT-TELCO mission.
Everything is online, available at any hour.
The guides let other educational communities replicate it.
Technical and civic skills: networks, security and open work.

dashboard.seoDesc: Telemetry of the ESTRATOSAT-TELCO simulated mission and network simulator.
dashboard.title: Dashboard
dashboard.lead: Observe a simulated or calculated mission and experiment with network parameters.
dashboard.simulated: If no hardware is transmitting, the system plays a simulated flight (ascending to 30 km and descending) so you can explore the panel at any time.
dashboard.piData: Real data transmitted by Raspberry Pi 3+ via VPN
dashboard.autoOptimization: Automatic recommendation of SF and BW
dashboard.connectionError: Could not connect to the simulation service.
dashboard.dopplerChartLabel: Doppler shift during a satellite pass
dashboard.dopplerDescription: A CubeSat passing over the station shifts the received frequency:
dashboard.lossChartLabel: Power chart over the last points
dashboard.seekMaxDataRate: Seeks the highest data rate that keeps at least 10 dB of margin with current power, gains and distance.
dashboard.simulatorDescription: Move the controls and observe how the link between the balloon and the ground station changes. The simulation service calculates with the Friis model and LoRa sensitivity.
dashboard.stepEvolution: Evolution of the pass (from horizon to horizon)
dashboard.piNotTransmitting: The Pi is not transmitting yet. Connect the Pi via VPN and wait for it to send telemetry.
dashboard.noRealLaunch: No real launch has been performed yet. Connect the LoRa modules and sensors to see flight data.
dashboard.autoOptimizationDesc: Asks the service for the SF/BW combination with the highest data rate that maintains a target margin.
dashboard.fragileMargin: A margin of less than ~6 dB is fragile: weather or an antenna orientation change could cut the link.
dashboard.friisEquation: Link budget step by step (Friis equation)
dashboard.highSf: High SF: more range, less speed.
dashboard.tryHigherSf: Try increasing the SF (higher SF = more sensitivity but lower data rate).

sections.d: Balloon inflation, final payload verification and release with telemetry already active.
The balloon crosses the troposphere and enters the stratosphere while the LoRa link is maintained.
Near 30 km, altitude, pressure, temperature and link quality are recorded.
Parachute descent and payload location using the last received position.

sectionExtras.satellites: Three educational platforms at a glance (typical values)
sectionExtras.cansatDesc: Model the size of a beverage can (~330 ml)
sectionExtras.cansatWhere: Rocket or small balloon, up to a few km
sectionExtras.lora: LoRa vs WiFi and LTE (typical orientative values)
sectionExtras.atmosphereLabel: Atmosphere layers infographic: troposphere, stratosphere and ozone layer, with a HAB balloon at 30 km
sectionExtras.habDescription: A HAB balloon rises to the stratosphere (~30 km): there the pressure is a small fraction of sea level and the temperature is around −50 °C, conditions that resemble space at a fraction of the cost.
sectionExtras.cubesatDescription: A CubeSat, on the other hand, orbits in LEO at about 400 km, inside the thermosphere, and moves at ≈ 7.7 km/s: that is where the Doppler effect studied in section 2.3 comes from.
sectionExtras.simulatorDescription: In the simulator you can change the orbital altitude and frequency and see the Doppler shift against the LoRa receiver tolerance.
sectionExtras.source: Source: systematic literature review (PRISMA 2020) that supports this ODC.
